overall: The AG found the Swansea Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve April 23 open session minutes and executive session minutes from four meetings; it found no intentional violation and no violation on the May 28 purpose statement.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to approve its April 23 open session minutes in a timely manner, with the minutes not approved until May 28.
allegations.key_passage: Having shown no good cause for delay, and having failed to approve the April 23 meeting minutes by May 23, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve the April 23 minutes.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to approve executive session minutes for December 11, 2018, April 16, April 23, and May 28 in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: we find the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve meeting minutes for executive sessions held on December 11, 2018; April 16; April 23; and May 28.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly failed to state the detrimental-effect statement when moving into executive session at the May 28 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board entered executive session on May 28 only under Purpose 2, no statement regarding a detrimental effect was required.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged failure to approve minutes for executive sessions on December 18, 2018 and April 30.
allegations.key_passage: a review of the available minutes indicates that no executive sessions were held on these dates.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the late minute approvals were an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find that the Board acted to intentionally violate the Law in this instance.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued in a request for further review that the Town Administrator lacked authorization to respond for the Board.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation because it was not raised in the original complaint.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Each Board member to review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law training video on minutes and certify in writing to the Division of Open Government within 30 days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order each member of the Board to certify in writing to the Division of Open Government within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter, using the form attached, that he has complied with this order.
